newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling gains slightly against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling gains slightly against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling rose marginally on Wednesday in calm trade as expected inflows from the agricultural sector failed to materialise, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.99 against the dollar from 56 on Tuesday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.55 from 87.53 on Tuesday.
A commercial banker said there was no clearing house on Wednesday as the central bank remained closed for lunch hosted in honour of President Daniel arap Moi.
"Calm conditions prevailed in the market as the anticipated forex inflows from the agricultural sector turned out to be minimal," a dealer said.

"Trade was confined to the 55.95/05 range throughout the day with little interest from either side of the prices," he said. "This trend is set to continue as the week is interrupted by a local market holiday tommorrow (Thursday)."
Dealers said overnight money market rates dipped to levels of between 12 and 18 percent from between 15 and 20 percent on Tuesday.
